mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLK 200 or 250 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M271 engine for the GLK 200 or 250 costs £2,950-£4,350 supply-only. Fitting adds £700-£1,300 depending on complexity - supercharged engine work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes GLK 200 or 250 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rattling noises may be heard after a cold start in M271 engines. This may be caused by wear of the chain drive, sprockets, or elongation of the timing chain. This can lead to incorrect timings and, in the worst case, to engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLK 200 or 250 petrol engine (M271) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M271 is a generally reliable engine when properly maintained. However, it has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch before 100,000 kilometres, camshaft timing gear failure, and supercharger coupling wear. All are manageable with the right maintenance schedule and proactive attention.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLK 200 and 250 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M271 engines routinely reach 120,000-150,000 miles before major work is needed. With timely timing chain service and regular maintenance, these engines demonstrate good longevity.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLK 200 or 250 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLK is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt M271 costs £2,950-£4,350 - comparable to or less than replacing a £4,000-£10,000 vehicle, especially when factoring in the cost of finding a comparable replacement SUV.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLK 200 or 250 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M271 requires approximately 5.5 litres with filter.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLK Class 200/250 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLK 200 and 250 petrol models launched with the X204 generation in 2008, powered by the M271 1.8-litre supercharged four-cylinder petrol engine - a compact, high-revving unit that delivered 184hp in the GLK 200 and 204hp in the GLK 250. The M271 engine family, introduced in 2002, featured a cast aluminium block, aluminium DOHC cylinder heads with 4 valves per cylinder, and variable valve timing. Production continued through the 2012 facelift until the X204 ended production in 2015.

milestones.description: Facelift X204; M271.860 continues with improved timing chain components
End of X204 production; GLK replaced by GLC

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz GLK Class 200 and 250 petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M271 timing chain stretch to supercharger coupling wear and camshaft timing gear failure.

items.title: 1.8L Supercharged Petrol (2008-2015)
items.commonFailure: Timing chain stretch and tensioner failure - the M271's most notorious weakness. Many units experience chain stretch before reaching 100,000 kilometres (62,000 miles), causing noisy cold starts. Rattling noises after a cold start indicate wear of the chain drive, sprockets, or elongation of the timing chain, which can lead to incorrect timings and, in the worst case, engine damage. Camshaft timing gear failure is another common issue, causing sluggish acceleration, noticeable power loss, and poor throttle response. Typical failure mileage: 40,000-85,000 miles.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLK Class 200/250 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M271 supercharged engine delivers brisk acceleration and reasonable running costs, but it has well-documented weak points that drive replacement enquiries. The single most critical failure is timing chain stretch - a problem so common that many units experience it before 100,000 kilometres. Supercharger coupling wear and camshaft timing gear failure follow closely behind. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points - improved timing chain tensioners and reinforced camshaft timing gears - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.group: M271 Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Failure
problems.h4: M271 Timing Chain Stretch & Tensioner Failure - The Most Critical GLK Petrol Failure
problems.rootCause: The M271 timing chain stretches over time, especially on earlier models. The plastic timing chain guides can also wear down, exacerbating the issue. The main cause is usually extended oil change intervals or low-quality oil. Rattling noises may be heard after a cold start, caused by wear of the chain drive, sprockets, or elongation of the timing chain. If ignored, this can lead to incorrect timings and, in the worst case, engine damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2008-2015 GLK 200 or 250 petrol 4MATIC is worth approximately £4,000-£10,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLK 200/250 petrol sits in the £4,000-£10,000 band - replacement cost is typically justified for well-maintained examples, though owners of higher-mileage or lower-value examples should carefully evaluate repair costs against vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your GLK 200 or 250 exhibits a rattling noise on cold start, act immediately. The M271's timing chain is accessible with the engine in situ for tensioner and chain replacement. Specialist pricing of £1,100-£1,700 for a full chain kit is significantly lower than dealer rates. Most four-cylinder chains (M271/M274) are a one-day job at a specialist. However, if the engine has already suffered timing jump or valve damage, a minor repair is a financial risk. We recommend a fully rebuilt M271 unit, which includes the upgraded tensioner as standard and resolves all pre-facelift weak points.

problems.group: M271 Camshaft Timing Gear & Supercharger Coupling Wear
problems.h4: M271 Camshaft Timing Gear & Supercharger Coupling Wear - Boost Loss and Power Reduction
problems.rootCause: One of the most notorious problems of the M271 engine is the failure of the camshaft timing gears. Symptoms include sluggish acceleration, noticeable loss of power, and poor throttle response. The supercharger coupling bearings also wear out simultaneously. Combined boost loss and timing drift quickly lead to poor compression and piston-to-valve contact.

problems.recommendation: The camshaft timing gear and supercharger failures are deeply linked. If your GLK 200 or 250 exhibits boost lag alongside timing rattle, separate repairs will only postpone inevitable failure. A rebuilt M271 unit resolves both systems simultaneously, offering better long-term economics than piecemeal dealer interventions.

problems.h4: M271 Oil Leaks & Thermostat Failure - Hidden Cost Traps
problems.rootCause: The M271 can suffer from oil leaks from the camshaft magnet seals and crankcase breather valve blockage, increasing oil consumption. Thermostat failure causing low running temperature and check engine light is also common. The ventilation hose with a built-in check valve that sends blow-by gas to the intake can become damaged and broken due to continuous exposure to heat and oil contamination.

problems.recommendation: Camshaft magnet oil leaks on the M271 are common but not usually urgent. If you notice oil around the camshaft magnets or experience misfires, have a specialist inspect the seals immediately. Thermostat failure is also common - if your GLK 200 or 250 takes longer than usual to warm up, budget £250-£450 for replacement.
